patterns.distinction: A structured hypothesis inventory across categories, rather than one omitted influence.

sources.title: I Beg to Differ

patterns.title: Iceberg Model

How do I move from an event to the arrangements behind it?
I want to separate a recurring pattern from my explanation of it.

patterns.title: Abstraction Laddering

sources.title: LUMA Institute's abstraction laddering reference

patterns.distinction: Returns from a broader purpose through alternative means, instead of stopping at the higher goal.

practice.title: Climb and Return

example_user_queries: We are arguing about a requested solution before its purpose is clear.

How do I return from a broad goal to a testable option?
I know what I want to build but not what it should enable.
Which level of framing gives us useful room to invent?

How can I ask why without becoming too abstract to act?
I want different concrete ways to achieve the same purpose.

patterns.title: Decision Matrix
patterns.originator_or_source: Weighted multi-criteria comparison is a broad decision-analysis tradition; ASQ documents this form. Not all weighted matrices are Pugh datum matrices.

patterns.title: Productive Thinking Model
patterns.originator_or_source: Tim Hurson, Think Better: An Innovator’s Guide to Productive Thinking (2007). Original introductory application, not an official program.

sources.title: Tim Hurson: Think Better

patterns.distinction: A connecting overview coordinates distinct thinking jobs and explicit handoffs between them.

practice.title: Develop a Possibility Into a Plan
practice.interface: No external input required; result is a typed record of context, method-specific records, review, and next commitment.
practice.limits: Participant-led judgments and plans; no external action, diagnosis, or scheduled follow-up.
practice.useful_outputs: Situation, success criteria and generative question; options and ranked whole records; developed solution; resource and review plan.

practice.result_expression: {situation: situation, success: success, question: question, options: options, priorities: priorities, solution: develop, resource_plan: resources}

visual.alt_text: Six thinking jobs connect the courtyard concern to a trial: understand use, describe success, frame a question, generate options, develop a proposal, and align resources. A dashed return from the storage question reopens development.
visual.caption: The courtyard proposal moves through six different thinking jobs. If storage is unavailable, return to development instead of treating the plan as settled.
visual.rationale: The figure distinguishes thinking jobs and makes the return from a resource discovery to solution development explicit.

example_user_queries: We jump from a vague concern to our first solution.

patterns.title: Inversion
patterns.originator_or_source: A general mathematical and practical reasoning tradition, not a technique with one established inventor. Related application: Gary Klein’s project premortem.

sources.title: Gary Klein: Performing a Project Premortem

patterns.distinction: Includes bad-design construction and negative requirements; a premortem assumes a favored plan has already failed.

practice.title: Design the Failure, Then Remove Its Causes
practice.interface: No external input required; result is a typed record of context, method-specific records, review, and next commitment.
practice.limits: Participant-led judgments and plans; no external action, diagnosis, or scheduled follow-up.
practice.useful_outputs: Desired and unwanted outcomes; possible failure mechanisms, evidence and countermeasures; safeguards and positive-design check.
practice.output_kind: record; nested fields inferred and checked by the Pattern Language compiler
practice.result_expression: {aim: context, failure_mechanisms: mechanisms, design: review}

visual.rationale: The worked negative-to-positive reasoning makes the move explicit without a decorative opposite-arrow image.

example_user_queries: How could we reliably create the outcome we want to avoid?
I want safeguards before a detailed plan exists.

use_when: How could we reliably create the outcome we want to avoid?
I want safeguards before a detailed plan exists.

patterns.title: First-principles Thinking
patterns.originator_or_source: Long philosophical and scientific tradition, including Aristotle’s Physics, Book I. No modern sole inventor asserted.

sources.title: Aristotle: Physics, Book I

patterns.distinction: Requires a constructive solution grounded in retained facts, rather than only challenging assumptions.

patterns.title: Issue Trees
patterns.originator_or_source: Logic-tree tradition in structured problem solving; documented by Charles Conn and Hugo Sarrazin in McKinsey’s problem-solving discussion. No sole inventor asserted.

sources.title: Charles Conn and Hugo Sarrazin: How to master the seven-step problem-solving process

patterns.distinction: Builds an explicit investigation structure with coverage checks and prioritized leaves.

practice.title: Build an Investigation Tree
practice.interface: No external input required; result is a typed record of context, method-specific records, review, and next commitment.
practice.limits: Open collections are bounded for a focused first pass. Participant-entered relationship or parent names require manual checking.

practice.output_kind: record; nested fields inferred and checked by the Pattern Language compiler
practice.result_expression: {root: root, branches: branches, leaves: leaves, review: review}

patterns.title: Balancing Feedback Loops

sources.title: The Systems Thinker: Reinforcing and Balancing Loops
Donella Meadows: Leverage Points
